What is stored where

These pages are static files. There is no server behind them, so there is nowhere for your progress to go unless you send it. Everything below lives in the browser you are reading this in, and nothing about you leaves this device without your explicit action — an export you download, a share you press, or a sharing consent you turn on.

One rule

Nothing leaves this device without your opt-in

  • No page here makes a network request about you. The only files read unprompted are the page's own scripts, its catalogue and auth-config.json beside the homepage, all same-origin.
  • Sign-in providers are contacted only when a deployment configured them, and only when you press their button (docs/sign-in.md). With nothing configured, no provider is ever contacted.
  • An export is a file handed to you. You decide where it goes.

Who the stores belong to

StateWhere progress is keptWhat happens to it
Not signed in ("This device")localStorage, the original keysStays until you clear it. The first sign-in on this device records it once as the "This device" profile — in place, never moved, never deleted.
Signed inlocalStorage, every key suffixed ::id-<digest>The digest is a salted fold of your learner id; no e-mail address, wallet address or provider subject is ever part of a key. Signing out hides it; another person on the same device sees their own.
Free demosessionStorage, suffixed ::demoEnds with the tab. Nothing is written to localStorage. Signing in offers to keep the demo runs — an explicit button, off unless pressed.

The stores

KeyHoldsLeaves the device
vr-training-records-v1One entry per finished attempt: station, category, score, stars, corrections, unsafe actions, time against par, pass or fail, the crew tag you typed. No biometrics, no free text beyond that tag.Only in an export you download (CSV, xAPI, Open Badges, transcript).
vr-passport-v1Which world an award came from, which job boards are done, which returns were paid.Only in an export.
vr-training-episodes-v1The optional step-by-step episode log for robot-training datasets; the crew tag is folded to a digest before it is written.Only through the consent-gated share (docs/wallets-and-sharing.md).
bayworld-career-v1, underwater-career-v1, redwood-career-v1, the quest and dive storesEach world's reputation, credits, quest steps and activities.Never.
vr-treasures-v1Which treasures you have found.Never.
vr-training-signoffs-v1Instructor attestations typed on this device: a name, a date, a note.Only in a transcript export.
vr-training-auth-v1The signed-in session: display name, provider, the id the provider returned. Removed on sign-out.Posted only to the host page a deployment configured as homePage, never to anyone else.
vr-org-v1The organisation layer (docs/enterprise.md): organisations, cohorts, members with a display name and a role, your progress-sharing consent (off by default), a data-minimised progress snapshot when it is on, and this device's audit log of coordinator actions.Only in a cohort file a coordinator exports, and then only the snapshots of members who turned sharing on.
holodeck-lang-v1, vr-training-profile-salt-v1, vr-training-profiles-v1Your language, the random salt the digests use, the "This device" adoption note.Never.

What an organisation can see

Cohorts, consent and the coordinator

  • You join a cohort with an invite code and a display name you type — initials are fine. Nobody is added to a cohort by an identity they did not type themselves.
  • Your progress is shared with the cohort's coordinator only after you turn sharing on, and only as a snapshot per station: best stars, unsafe actions, interruptions handled and missed, number of attempts, the date of the last attempt. No debrief text, no crew tag, no sign-in id.
  • Turning sharing off removes the snapshot from this device's store. A file already exported is the coordinator's copy, as any file you hand over would be.
  • Every export, import and role change a coordinator makes is written to an audit log kept on that device and shown in the instructor console.
  • A completion certificate is a page rendered from that snapshot and marked "prototype — not a credential". It is not a licence, a card or a certification.

Deployment settings

A deployment for one organisation may fill in the enterprise block of auth-config.json: the organisation's name, which sign-in methods are offered, a default language, which worlds and programmes are enabled, and a data-retention note it writes for itself. Nothing in that block is read from a link, and single sign-on remains a configuration point on the host page — no identity provider is built into these files. See docs/enterprise.md.

Clearing this browser's site data removes every store above. Inside the sign-in dialog, Sign out and clear my records removes only the signed-in person's records. Back to the homepage.
